summary.text: A 36-year-old woman with hypertension treated with enalapril, mild preeclampsia in her first pregnancy and right lower extremity DVT in her second pregnancy presented to the emergency department with 48 hours of progressively worsening dyspnea, severe mesogastric abdominal pain and headache. She was afebrile with SpO2 88% on 36% FiO2, pulse 90/min and blood pressure 150/100 mmHg.

Presentation labs showed positive lupus anticoagulant, aCL IgG 65 GPL U/mL (reference < 20) and anti-β2GPI IgG 22 U/mL (normal < 20). CT showed pulmonary artery thrombosis consistent with bilateral pulmonary embolism, substantial left renal infarction, partial celiac trunk thrombosis and aortic thrombus extending into the left renal and celiac arteries.

APS was diagnosed and CAPS suspected; TTP, HUS, DIC and HIT were judged less likely given no thrombocytopenia (platelets 252 × 109/L), no hemolytic anemia, normal coagulation studies and no prior heparin exposure.

Therapeutic plasma exchange was considered but not performed because the institution lacked resources. After nephrology and vascular surgery consultation she received intravenous methylprednisolone 80 mg/day and intravenous immunoglobulin 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days, and on the day of admission underwent radical open left nephrectomy for complete renal necrosis and to remove a potential infection source.

Post-operatively she had brief amaurosis and right homonymous hemianopsia; cerebral CT showed a left occipital ischemic event and right cerebellar hypodensities/ischemic stroke, and CAPS was strongly supported with the pre-operative elevated aPL.

She was admitted to the ICU for rapid deterioration, developed multi-organ failure needing hemodynamic support and mechanical ventilation, and had gradual resolution of organ failures. Burkholderia cepacia bacteremia responded to a 10-day course of trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole.
After reaching the INR target of 2.0-3.0 she was discharged on warfarin. At a follow-up visit 3 months after initial testing aPL remained positive, INR was 2.3 and she remained asymptomatic.
